quickGuide.title: Quick Guide
quickGuide.heroSubtitle: Follow the steps below to create your first machine learning model in PredictSys AI
quickGuide.tipText: At any time, you can open the project's AI Assistant to request simple explanations about what was done, the metrics, and next steps.

1.title: Create a new project
1.content:
Click "New Project" and fill in:
• Project name (e.g., "Customer churn prediction")
• Description of what you want to predict
• Business objective in simple language
• Problem type: Classification (0/1) or Regression (numeric value)

2.title: Upload your data (CSV)
2.content:
In the "Data" step, upload a CSV file with your information.
PredictSys will automatically detect numeric and categorical columns and show a preview of the first rows.

3.title: Understand your dataset (EDA)
3.content:
In the "Analysis (EDA)" step, click "Calculate EDA".
You'll see statistics and charts that help understand your data: value distribution, most frequent categorical variables, missing data, etc.

4.title: Choose target variable and features
4.content:
In the "Variables" step, select the column you want to predict (target variable) and which columns will be used as model input (features).
If in doubt, the AI Assistant can explain each metric and concept.

5.title: Train the model
5.content:
In the "Training" step, click "Train models".
PredictSys automatically tests different algorithms and presents a table comparing AUC, F1, Precision, Recall, and Accuracy (for classification) or MAE/RMSE/R² (for regression).

6.title: Deploy the model to production
6.content:
Choose the best model and publish to production with 1 click.
In "API & Deploy" you'll find the prediction endpoint and examples of how to integrate your system.

documentation.title: Documentation
documentation.introText: PredictSys AI is a predictive models platform focused on tabular data. It allows business users to create machine learning projects without writing code, going through data, analysis, training, and deployment stages in a guided manner.

project.desc: Set of data, modeling, and results for a specific business objective (e.g., "Churn prediction in the journey").

dataset.desc: CSV file with customer history, transactions, or events.

target.desc: What you want to predict (e.g., churn_90d, purchase value, default).

features.desc: Columns used as model input (customer age, number of purchases, channel, etc.).

eda.desc: Exploratory Analysis that shows statistics and charts about the data.

production.desc: Chosen model to be used by the prediction API.

flowSteps.1: Project information: Name, description, objective, and problem type.
flowSteps.2: Data upload: Upload a CSV file with your historical data.
flowSteps.3: Exploratory analysis (EDA): Visualize statistics and charts of your data.
flowSteps.4: Variable selection: Choose the target variable and input features.
flowSteps.5: Training: The platform automatically trains multiple algorithms.
flowSteps.6: Deploy: Publish the chosen model and get the prediction API.

metrics.AUC: Measures how well the model can separate churners from non-churners across all possible thresholds. Ranges from 0 to 1: the closer to 1, the better. Good metric when data is imbalanced (few churns).
metrics.F1: Harmonic mean between Precision and Recall. Summarizes in one number the balance between: how many predicted churns are actually churns (Precision) and how many actual churns the model found (Recall).
metrics.Precision: Of all customers the model said will churn, what percentage actually churned. Useful when the cost of reaching someone who won't churn is high.
metrics.Recall: Of all customers who actually churned, what percentage the model identified as churn. Useful when it's very important NOT to miss churns.
metrics.Accuracy: Total percentage of correct predictions, considering churn and non-churn. Can be misleading if the base is very imbalanced (almost no one churning).
metrics.MAE: Mean absolute difference between predicted and actual values. Shows, on average, how much the model errs up or down, in the same unit as the target variable.
metrics.MSE: Mean of squared errors. Penalizes large errors more heavily. Useful for comparing models, but not as intuitive for business.
metrics.RMSE: Square root of MSE. In the same unit as the target variable and also penalizes large errors significantly.
metrics.R2: Measures how much of the target variation the model explains (0 to 1). The closer to 1, the more the model explains the variable's behavior.

q1.question: Do I need to know how to code to use PredictSys?
q1.answer: No! PredictSys AI was created to be 100% no-code. All steps are done through buttons, forms, and visual selections. You don't need to write any code.

q2.question: What file format is accepted?
q2.answer: We currently accept CSV files (comma-separated values) with UTF-8 encoding. It's the most common format for exporting data from spreadsheets and systems.

q3.question: How many rows can my dataset have?
q3.answer: The file can be up to 50 MB. For model training, we use up to 5,000 rows to ensure processing is fast and efficient.

q4.question: Can I use the platform for cases other than churn?
q4.answer: Yes! PredictSys works for any classification problem (predicting categories, like yes/no, A/B/C) or regression (predicting numeric values, like sales, price). Examples: default, purchase propensity, sales forecast, credit score.

q5.question: How does the prediction API work?
q5.answer: After publishing a model to production, you get a REST API endpoint. Just send input data in JSON format and receive the prediction as a response. Code examples are provided in the 'API & Deploy' tab.
